svg.title: Open service loop mark, reversed (provisional)
svg.desc: PROVISIONAL working mark. An asymmetric four-stage OPEN LOOP. The four stages sit ON the pathway itself. The curve starts inside stage 1 and ends inside the accent stage, so no node floats free, and the loop never closes: the opening between the accent stage and stage 1 is the point. Deterministic geometry, constructed from the polar table below and written out as literal coordinates. Nothing here is traced from, or embedded as, raster art. Construction (viewBox 64): loop centre (30.17,31.58), stroke 6.4, round caps. The radius VARIES with angle, so the silhouette is an organic pebble rather than a circle and deliberately not a status or loading ring. Polar samples, in the order the path travels them (angle deg, radius): 55/19.6* 80/20.5 110/21.2 132/20.9 157/20.1* 186/18.9 216/18.1 250/17.7 274/17.9 292/18.4* 316/19.8 334/21.2 350/22.8* Starred samples carry a stage node: 55deg r 6.0 - 157deg r 6.9 (heaviest) - 292deg r 5.9 - 350deg r 6.6 (accent, on the widest radius, closing the path). The curve is a Catmull-Rom spline through those samples, emitted as cubics. Reversed: for Forge Black and other dark surfaces. The pathway goes white; the endpoint keeps Burnt Orange.
